channel.title: NotchPop
channel.description: Updates for NotchPop — your MacBook notch, but useful.

item.title: v1.5.24
item.description:
• Screenshot drops work now. The drop handler only listened for .fileURL — but the macOS screenshot floating thumbnail (the bottom-right preview after ⇧⌘5) ships PNG bytes BEFORE auto-saving, so dragging from there had nothing for us to load. Now also accepts .image / .png / .tiff — image-data drops get written to ~/Library/Application Support/NotchPop/shelf/screenshot-yyyy-MM-dd-HHmmss-SSS.png and shelfed as a real file. Web drags + Photos drags work the same way.
  • One-click 'download new version' notification. The independent-launch version check posts a notification when you're behind, but in v1.5.19–v1.5.23 clicking it did nothing. Now AppDelegate is the UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate — clicking the banner opens the GitHub-release DMG URL directly in your default browser. Drag to Applications, replace, done. Sparkle-stuck users finally have a one-click escape.

item.title: v1.5.23
item.description: • Clipboard copy actually copies now. Previous code did clearContents() + setString() and ignored setString's Bool return. From the .nonactivatingPanel notch, that two-step sometimes races with macOS's pasteboard server (especially with Universal Clipboard syncing) — setString silently returns false and the pasteboard ends up empty (cleared in step 1, never re-filled in step 2). User-visible result: 'it just didnt copy.' Fix: writeStringRobustly() now uses declareTypes + setString as the primary path, falls back to writeObjects([NSString]) if that returns false, verifies by reading back, and retries once after 50ms if neither path landed. Both attempts log to Console.

item.title: v1.5.22
item.description:
• App Shortcuts (new tab — 13th widget). Pin any macOS app or URL — click a tile, app opens. Manage in Settings → Shortcuts (NSOpenPanel for apps, type a URL for web links). Per user feedback: 'make it so you can connect it and make it open certain apps stuff like that.'
  • Connections — when X happens, do Y. Tiny automation engine. 9 triggers (Pomodoro focus start/end, break start/end, countdown end, charging start, music start/end, app launch); 5 actions (launch app, open URL, run macOS Shortcut, play sound, copy text). Wire 'when Pomodoro focus starts, launch Things 3' / 'when charging starts, play Sosumi' / 'when music ends, copy back-to-work message'. Test each trigger from Settings without waiting for a real event.

item.title: v1.5.21
item.description:
• Settings button in the notch now actually works. It WAS opening the Settings panel, but the panel was being raised to .floating (level 3) while the notch sits at .statusBar+1 (level 26) — settings was rendered BEHIND the notch the moment the level dropped to .normal. Fixed by pinning the panel above the notch (.statusBar+2) and never lowering it.
  • Up/down arrows in Settings → Tabs are now reliable. Hit area was just the 11pt SF Symbol glyph — easy to miss. Now wrapped in 28×28 rounded-rect buttons with explicit contentShape, fade-on-disable instead of hide so the row layout stays consistent.
  • Clipboard click pastes for real. Default behavior is now: click a chip → copy to pasteboard AND synthesize ⌘V into the previously-frontmost app. Toggle in Settings → Tabs → Clipboard tab.
  • Timer progress bar no longer covered by the notch. The full-width progress capsule was hidden in the middle by the hardware notch cutout. Now split into LEFT and RIGHT segments mirroring the same progress fraction, with the cutout area left empty.
  • Pomodoro options inline. Click the duration chip in the Pomodoro tab — the popover now includes auto-start toggle, strict mode, long-break cycle stepper, daily goal stepper, and the sound picker with Preview. No more digging through Settings → Pomodoro for these.

item.title: v1.5.20
item.description:
• Music elapsed bug fixed. Track time was rolling 0→5→0→5 forever because the 5-second probe and most Spotify notifications didn't include 'Player Position' — they built a fresh track with elapsed=0 and overwrote the live-ticking value. publish() now preserves elapsed (and duration) when title+artist match the previous track and the incoming value is zero. Spotify's 'Player Position' / 'Position' fields are also parsed if present.
  • Close animation no longer choppy. Window resize is now animated via NSAnimationContext (0.32s ease-in-out) so it stays in sync with SwiftUI's spring. Before, the window jumped to its new size INSTANTLY while SwiftUI animated the inner shape over ~0.4s — content rendered at expanded size inside a suddenly-tiny window for a beat.
  • Welcome is way slower and cooler. The glow now ramps in via a 1.6s smoothstep envelope (slowly grows from a tight pulse around the notch to the full bloom), pulses gently, then fades out over the last 1s of the welcome window. Hue cycle dropped from 8s to 5s so you actually see the pink → purple → blue → mint rainbow during a typical 8s welcome.
  • Auto-replays welcome on every version bump. Each time you install a new version (or upgrade via Force Update Now), the welcome plays automatically once. No more 'I had to replay it.'
  • Welcome default duration bumped 5.5s → 8s with the new 3–15s slider range.

item.title: v1.5.19
item.description:
• Sparkle escape hatch — for real this time. Force Update Now now ALSO clears NSURLCache and calls SPUUpdater.resetUpdateCycle() (Sparkle's official 'throw away in-memory state' API). Plus the feed URL is appended with a per-launch cache-busting token so Cloudflare can't return a 304 with a stale parse.
  • Independent appcast check at launch. 8 seconds after launch, NotchPop fetches the appcast DIRECTLY (bypassing Sparkle entirely), parses the latest version with a regex, and posts a system notification if you're behind. Safety net for the cases where Sparkle's internal state is stuck.

item.title: v1.5.18
item.description:
• Hide the timer. New per-track toggle in Settings → Behavior so you can hide the running-timer pill without disabling music live activity (or vice versa). The timer keeps running — only the flanking surface goes away.
  • End-of-timer sound. Already shipped under Settings → Pomodoro → Sound, but now also surfaced via the master "Live activities" section so it's findable from Behavior too. Pomodoro phase end + Countdown timer end both call TimerSound.play() which respects your sound choice.
  • 15+ new options: show artwork in live activity (privacy mode), marquee scroll speed, Apple Music polling interval, shelf max items + thumbnails + click-action, calendar event count + time-range + hide all-day, weather refresh interval + wind toggle, notes font size + monospaced, clipboard history size, animation speed multiplier, and quiet hours (suppress peeks during a chosen time window).

item.title: v1.5.17
item.description:
• Welcome glow is finally visible. Replaced the subtle Ellipse-blur (which faded to ~zero opacity at the edges) with a 3-color SwiftUI .shadow() halo applied directly to the notch shape — shadows render outside the view frame and aren't clipped, so this guarantees the bloom shows up regardless of layout. Plus a 3-layer ZStack gradient backdrop with bigger 110pt side / 100pt bottom padding.
  • Replay welcome no longer lands off-center. When you click Replay, the view model now snaps to a clean baseline first (expanded=false, showingWelcome=false), waits one runloop tick, then flips showingWelcome=true, then 50ms later flips expanded=true with a spring. Avoids the race where applyContentSize ran with mid-flip state and centered for the wrong target size.
  • Welcome closes with an animation now. Both showingWelcome=false and expanded=false are wrapped in a single withAnimation block so the glow padding and the panel shrink together.
  • Tab bar no longer truncates. When you have more than 4 visible tabs, inactive tabs go icon-only with the active tab keeping its label. Override in Settings → Behavior → 'Always show tab labels'.
  • Album cover plays/pauses on click. Plus the breathing animation got 4× more visible (1% → 4% scale change).
  • 7 new settings: Always show tab labels, auto-collapse after tab select, welcome peek duration (3–12s slider), show menubar icon, show inline battery, show version label, charging peek toggle.

item.title: v1.5.16
item.description:
• Music seek works. Drag the playhead in the Music tab and release — it actually scrubs Apple Music or Spotify to that position now (used to be cosmetic-only). Works for both players via AppleScript.
  • Click outside to collapse is now wired up. Settings → Behavior toggle was already there but never connected — it is now, via a global mouse-down monitor (passive observation only, doesn't consume clicks).
  • New Weather tab. Live conditions from Open-Meteo (free, no API key, no rate limits). Big SF Symbol, temp + location, °F / °C toggle, refresh button. Updates every 15 minutes. Falls back to coarse IP-based location if you decline CoreLocation permission.

item.title: v1.5.15
item.description:
• Centering bug fixed. The notch was occasionally landing at the right position then jumping to the left a moment later — caused by an async race in the window controller (an older applyContentSize's stale newFrame would clobber a newer call's correct frame). Fixed with a per-call generation counter so only the latest re-apply runs.
  • Screen detection caches. ScreenHelper now caches the chosen display ID for the session, only re-resolving when display config changes. No more jumping between screens mid-session.
  • New Quick Actions tab — Lock, Sleep, Screenshot, Mission Control, plus one-tap shortcuts to Sound / Display / Network prefs and Trash.
  • Live activity progress line. Music's track elapsed and Pomodoro/Countdown phase progress now show as a thin gradient line at the bottom of the integrated notch pill.

item.title: v1.5.14
item.description:
• Welcome glow returns. Replay the welcome animation (Settings → About → Replay welcome animation) and you'll see a hue-cycling pink/purple/blue/mint halo bleeding OUT around the notch — the visual that was supposed to be there since v1.0 but kept getting clipped to the notch frame.
  • If you've turned on Reduce Motion (Appearance tab), the glow is static instead of pulsing.

item.title: v1.5.13
item.description:
• Settings now scrolls everywhere. Pre-1.5.13 only the Behavior and Pomodoro tabs scrolled — Tabs, World Clock, and About silently truncated their tail content. All eight tabs are scrollable now.
  • New Updates tab: Force Update Now button, current-version readout, last-checked timestamp, and a toggle for automatic checks. If Sparkle ever gets confused again, this is your panic button.
  • New Appearance tab: pick an accent color (pink/blue/purple/mint/orange/graphite or the brand pink→blue gradient), 12-vs-24-hour clock format, show seconds, reduce motion.
  • New Diagnostics tab: re-detect screen, re-center notch, copy diagnostic info to clipboard for bug reports, jump straight to Console.app.
  • New Behavior options: auto-expand on file drag, click-outside-to-collapse toggle.

item.title: v1.5.12
item.description:
• Fixed auto-update getting stuck. Sparkle no longer silently queues installs that never land — every new version prompts you explicitly. If you were trapped on an old version, this update fixes that.
  • New Force Update Now menubar item that wipes Sparkle's cached state and re-checks immediately. Use it any time auto-update gets weird.
  • Skipped-version markers from prior releases are now wiped on launch, so accidentally clicking 'Skip This Version' on an old release doesn't trap you forever.

item.title: v1.5.11
item.description:
v1.5.11 — Settings as NSPanel + centering diagnostics + timer presets + welcome replay in menu bar

Settings

v1.5.10's manual NSWindow approach kept failing for some users. Switched to a custom SettingsPanel: NSPanel subclass with canBecomeKey/Main overridden. NSPanels surface in LSUIElement (accessory) apps without needing the activation-policy flip dance that v1.5.10 was doing. Simpler code, more reliable.

Centering diagnostics

If the notch is STILL off-center after this update, open Console.app, search for NotchPop centering:, and the log will tell us exactly which screen got picked, what frame it has, and what frame the window was set to. Includes ALL screens for comparison so we can see whether ScreenHelper.notchedScreen() picked the right one. Also added a re-apply pass after macOS's async window placement in case it overrides our frame.

Quicker timer editing

The duration popover (click '25m' in the Pomodoro pane) now shows quick-pick chips: Focus → 15/20/25/30/45/50/60/90, Short break → 1/3/5/7/10/15, Long break → 10/15/20/25/30/45. Tap a chip to set + close. Stepper still there for custom values.

Replay welcome animation in the menu bar

Until Settings is fully reliable for everyone, you can replay the 3-scene gradient intro from the menu bar dropdown (look for the rectangle icon in the top-right of your screen). Same as the button buried in Settings → About.

item.title: v1.5.10
item.description:
v1.5.10 — Settings window: belt-and-suspenders

v1.5.9 built a manual NSWindow + NSHostingController for Settings — but apparently the window was being created but never SURFACED on your machine. Three more fixes in this version:

  • collectionBehavior includes .moveToActiveSpace — without this, on multi-Space setups the settings window can be created on a hidden Space and look like it 'didn't open.'
  • window.level temporarily boosted to .floating while ordering front, then dropped back to .normal after 0.3s — guarantees the window comes ABOVE the notch panel (which sits at .statusBar+1).
  • Activation policy flip is deferred to next runloop tick via DispatchQueue.main.async — on some macOS versions, makeKeyAndOrderFront silently fails if the policy is still mid-transition from .accessory to .regular.
  • NSLog diagnostics at every step (openSettings invoked, controller created, window ordered front with frame). If Settings still doesn't open after this, open Console.app and search for 'NotchPop' — the logs will show exactly where the chain breaks.

item.title: v1.5.9
item.description:
v1.5.9 — Settings + centering, real fixes this time

You said v1.5.8 still had the broken Settings button and the off-center notch. Both were fixed earlier (v1.5.4 and v1.5.7) but the underlying mechanisms had edge cases I missed:

Settings (now actually works)

SwiftUI's Settings { ... } Scene only registers showSettingsWindow: when the app has an NSMainMenu. We're an LSUIElement (menu-bar) app with no main menu, so NSApp.sendAction had nothing to dispatch to. Built a manual NSWindow + NSHostingController for the Settings window, bypassing the SwiftUI Settings scene entirely. Click the gear in the notch (or menubar → Settings…) and it actually opens now.

Centering (uses CGDisplayIsBuiltin now)

safeAreaInsets.top > 0 was the previous detection for 'this is the notched display.' On some hardware combos (multi-display setups, certain external monitors) this gave the wrong answer. Now using CGDisplayIsBuiltin() — the most authoritative API to identify the laptop's internal display. Three-tier fallback: built-in display first, safeAreaInsets second, primary screen third, NSScreen.main last.

item.title: v1.5.8
item.description:
v1.5.8 — Big polish drop (6 parallel agents)

Two new widgets

  • 📅 Calendar peek — today's next ~5 events from macOS Calendar via EventKit. Color stripes from each event's calendar. Permission-state-aware UI (Click-to-enable / Denied-with-instructions / Granted). Auto-refreshes when calendar data changes.
  • 🎧 AirPods battery — when AirPods are connected, shows L / R / Case battery in mini pills. Color-coded (green ≥50%, amber 20-49%, red <20%). Polls system_profiler every 60s. Handles AirPods Max single-side and pods-in-case nil cases.

Polish across the board

  • 🎵 Music — draggable scrubber knob, marquee-scrolling track title for long names, subtle 1.5s pulse on artwork while playing, monospaced timestamp (1:42 / 3:28), cleaner empty state.
  • ⚡ Charging peek — flowing electric-current animation along the battery fill, spark particles burst when % ticks up, splashier 28pt percentage with gradient fill. Inline indicator tightened to a clean 50pt pill, checkmark instead of bolt at 100%.
  • ⚙️ Settings — section headers (Startup / Default tab / Display / Hover timing / Notch fit / Durations / Flow / Sound / etc.), captions under every toggle, flush-right toggle alignment via LabeledContent, cleaner reorder arrows (hidden at boundaries), Reset all settings with confirmation in About → Danger zone, footer credit on every tab.
  • 🌐 Website — refreshed hero, demo, features grid, comparison table for v1.5.x reality. Version pill in release-meta line.

Tab pool now 10 widgets

Shelf · Music · Pomodoro · Timers · World Clock · Notes · Clipboard · System · Calendar · AirPods. New ones default to OFF — toggle on in Settings → Tabs.

item.title: v1.5.7
item.description:
v1.5.7 — CRITICAL fix: auto-update was infinitely looping

The bug

Every release I've shipped (v1.5.1 through v1.5.6) had CFBundleShortVersionString = 1.0 internally. release.sh was bumping Info.plist with PlistBuddy, but xcodegen regenerates Info.plist on every build from project.yml — and project.yml didn't list a version, so each build reset it to 1.0. Sparkle saw users on '1.0', told them v1.5.6 was available, installed v1.5.6 (which also reported 1.0), and said 'update available!' all over again. Endless loop.

The fix

  • Added MARKETING_VERSION as a build setting in project.yml — it's now the source of truth.
  • Added CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION) to project.yml's info.properties so xcodegen interpolates it.
  • release.sh now seds MARKETING_VERSION in project.yml directly, so the next xcodegen+xcodebuild produces a bundle that ACTUALLY reports the right version.
  • Verified: NotchPop.app/Contents/Info.plist for this build correctly shows 1.5.7.

Centering also fixed

NotchPop was using NSScreen.main which returns whichever screen has keyboard focus — so the notch UI wandered to whichever monitor you last clicked. Now ScreenHelper.notchedScreen() prefers the screen with an actual hardware notch (your built-in MacBook display), falling back to the primary screen.

What you'll notice after this update

This is the LAST time you'll see 'update available' on a loop. From v1.5.7 onward, Sparkle correctly knows you're on v1.5.7 and will only prompt when there's a genuinely newer release.

item.title: v1.5.6
item.description:
v1.5.6 — Timer end-sound (with picker + preview)

  • Bug fix: the existing 'Sound effects' toggle wasn't actually wired to the timers — both Pomodoro and Countdown were unconditionally calling NSSound.beep() regardless of the setting. Now they go through a shared TimerSound helper that honors the toggle.
  • Sound picker in Settings → Pomodoro: choose between Beep (the system alert sound) and 11 of macOS's built-in named sounds — Glass, Submarine, Bell, Hero, Funk, Frog, Pop, Sosumi, Tink, Ping, Purr. Default is Glass (same chime macOS uses for Calendar alerts).
  • Preview button next to the picker — clicking it always plays the chosen sound, even if the master toggle is off, so you can audition before committing.
  • The single setting applies to both Pomodoro phase ends and the Countdown timer.
  • Cleaned up Settings: the old 'Sound effects' toggle in Behavior was redundant; removed it with a pointer to Pomodoro pane instead.

item.title: v1.5.5
item.description:
v1.5.5 — Centered notch + tighter hover + timer live preview + advancing progress bar

  • Notch is now actually centered over the hardware notch. applyContentSize was using window.frame.midX which drifts as the window resizes asymmetrically. Switched to screen.frame.midX so the visible shape is locked to the screen center, regardless of how wide the live activity makes it.
  • Hover is much less twitchy. The 18pt invisible hover gutter beneath the notch was triggering accidentally any time you moved past the top of the screen. Cut to 4pt — your mouse now has to actually be on the notch shape to open it.
  • Timer live preview now actually appears. The Pomodoro / Countdown live activity wasn't re-rendering when the timer started. Fixed by adding objectWillChange.send() on the relevant Combine sinks (pomodoro.$running, countdown.$running) so SwiftUI knows to re-evaluate the live activity body.
  • Music progress bar now advances. Added a 1-second local elapsed-advance timer that bumps track.elapsed while playing. The 5-second AppleScript probe still re-syncs to the real value periodically.
  • Pomodoro remaining and Countdown remaining changes also force re-renders so the live preview's countdown text ticks every second.

item.title: v1.5.4
item.description:
v1.5.4 — NotchNook-style live activities + bug fixes

What changed

  • Live activity is now ONE integrated wide pill — matching the NotchNook reference design. The notch grows wider with the icon on the left and content on the right (animated audio bars for music, countdown text for timer). Single continuous black shape, not two flanking pills.
  • Music: now shows actual play state — case-insensitive parsing of 'Playing' / 'Paused' / 'Stopped' so macOS 26's variant codes don't slip through as 'paused'. Optimistic state flip when you click the play button so the icon updates instantly.
  • Music: artwork loads via three paths — raw AppleScript data, then 'data of artwork 1', then a fallback that queries iTunes Search API for the cover (works without Apple Events permission).
  • Settings opens reliably — switched from NSApp.responds(to:) probing to NSApp.sendAction which goes through the responder chain SwiftUI's Settings scene actually listens to.
  • Settings gear in the notch — small ⚙ button next to the battery indicator in the expanded view. One click opens Settings.
  • Version label in the notch — small v1.5.4 tag in the top-right of the expanded view so you always know what you're on.
  • Drag-to-shelf forces Shelf visible — even if you've hidden the Shelf tab, dragging a file in temporarily adds it back so you have a real drop target.

Note

If music isn't detected, check System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation → NotchPop and make sure Music + Spotify are checked. macOS only prompts once and silent-denies forever after.

item.title: v1.5.3
item.description:
v1.5.3 — Drag-to-shelf is way easier now

  • Drop zone is now the entire window, not just the visible notch shape. You no longer have to aim at a 178pt sliver — anywhere near the top of the screen counts.
  • Auto-expand on drag-hover — the moment you start dragging a file toward the notch, it expands to the full Shelf view. Big drop target waiting for you instead of a tiny pill.
  • Visible drop ring — pink → blue gradient stroke appears around the notch while you're dragging so you know it's targeted.
  • Drag leaves the window without dropping → notch collapses back after a brief grace period.

item.title: v1.5.2
item.description:
v1.5.2 — Live activities

  • 🎵 Music pill — when something is playing in Apple Music or Spotify, a slim pill appears just to the right of the collapsed notch with album art + scrolling track title. Tap to open the Music tab.
  • ⏱ Timer pill — when Pomodoro or Countdown is running, the time-remaining pill sits to the left of the notch. Pomodoro takes priority and shows the phase emoji + a tiny progress arc. Tap to open the Pomodoro/Timers tab.
  • Toggle the whole feature in Settings → Behavior → Live activities.
  • This is the first auto-updated release — if you're on v1.5.1 you should see this install itself within ~4 hours, with system notifications.

item.title: v1.5.1
item.description:
v1.5.1 — Auto-update + bug fixes

  • 🚀 Auto-update via Sparkle — NotchPop checks for updates every 4 hours, signs them with EdDSA, and posts a system notification when an update is found / installed.
  • 🎵 Music probe fix — added NSAppleEventsUsageDescription so macOS Sequoia stops silently blocking AppleScript reads of Music/Spotify track info. Plus a 5-second re-probe covers songs that started after launch.
  • 📋 Clipboard widget · 🖥 System Stats widget · proper app icon · all carryover from v1.5.0.
